post.description:
Audit: writes [`audit::ADMIN_REFRESH`] with target
`"scope:all"`, `"org:<id>"`, or `"org:<id>;repo:<id>"`. The row
lands even on coalesce — the operator's *intent* is what we
audit, not whether a tick physically ran.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Narrow the tick to one org

parameters.name: repo_id
parameters.description: Narrow the tick to one repo (requires org_id)

get.summary: `GET /admin/runs` — paginated `dp_fetch_runs` projection.

post.description:
Calls [`Store::pseudonymise_user`], which rewrites
`login`/`email`/`name` to a `deleted-user-<short>` form and sets
`deleted_at`. The row id is preserved so historical reports
keep referential integrity (§0.5).

Audit: writes [`audit::USER_ANONYMISE`], target
`"user:<id>"`, **after** the cascade succeeds — a failed
cascade does not leave a misleading audit trail.

get.summary:
`GET /admin/users/:id/export` — chunked JSON dump of every row
dev-pulse holds about the user.
get.description:
Wire shape: a single JSON object matching [`UserExport`]. We
emit it incrementally so the process never holds more than one
page of event rows in memory at a time:

1. `{"user":<user>,"memberships":<memberships>,"events":[`
2. one JSON object per event, comma-separated, page by page
3. `]}`

Audit: writes [`audit::USER_EXPORT`], target `"user:<id>"`,
**before** streaming starts. Auditing pre-stream is deliberate
— the request was authorised, so the access attempt should be
recorded even if the network drops mid-stream.

post.summary: `POST /home-org` — atomically flip the user's home org.
post.description:
Postcondition (enforced by [`Store::set_home_org_for_user`]):
exactly one membership row per `user_id` has `home_org =
Some(org_id)` after this call returns.

Audit: writes one [`audit::HOME_ORG_SET`] row, `target =
"user:<user_id>"`. The row is written **after** the store flip
succeeds so a failed mutation doesn't leave a misleading audit
trail.

[`Store::set_home_org_for_user`]: dp_domain::store::Store::set_home_org_for_user

get.summary:
`GET /issues` — paginated, filterable issue list. Ordered by
`updated_at DESC` (matches GitHub's default "recently updated"
view).

post.description:
No CAS (there is no local row yet). Sequence:

1. Resolve `repo_id -> (Org, Repo)`.
2. §18.2 step 4 install-permission check.
3. Call the backend's `create_issue`.
4. Record the `issue.create` audit row (target = `repo_id#number`).

The fetcher / webhook receiver materialises the `dp_issues` row
on the next pass.

403.description: Writes not available for the target org

get.summary: `GET /issues/{id}` — single issue by id.

patch.summary:
`PATCH /issues/{id}` — update an existing GitHub issue. Routes
the `state` transition (open/closed) to the `issue.close` /
`issue.reopen` audit verbs; everything else is `issue.update`.

403.description: Writes not available for the target org

409.description: Stale local version — UI should reload

post.summary:
`POST /issues/{id}/comments` — append a comment. CAS-gated for
symmetry with PATCH so the UI's optimistic editor sees the same
stale-version surface.

403.description: Writes not available for the target org

409.description: Stale local version — UI should reload

get.summary:
`GET /issues/{id}/dates` — read the local `dp_issue_dates` row
for an issue. Returns `200 { issue_id, start_at: null, due_at:
null, … }` with all nullable fields set when no row exists, so
the frontend can render the picker uniformly. Authorisation:
the same `(issues, read)` pair the rest of the read surface uses
— read-only and per-org, the picker is also visible to viewers
who cannot write.

patch.summary:
`PATCH /issues/{id}/dates` — see module docs for the four-step
shape. Authorisation: `(issues, write)`.

403.description: Writes not available for the target org

get.summary:
`GET /issues/{id}/timeline` — newest-first activity strip for
one issue. The lookup uses the §6 guarded expression index on
`dp_activity_events` so the predicate is index-only even when
the parent repo has decades of accumulated history.

`GET /me/app-install-banner` — the §13.6 one-shot migration
banner data for the caller.
get.description:
* Reads memberships through `Store::list_memberships_for_user`
  so the §15.11 access gate is the only visibility check
  (out-of-org users get an empty `orgs` list — same as the
  `/orgs` directory surface).
* Per-org `writes_available` is the *same* verdict
  [`require_issues_write`] would return — no separate code
  path, no risk of the banner saying "you can write" while the
  write-gate disagrees.
* Not audited (read-only, no mutation).

200.description: Per-org App install status + §13.6 admin copy text

post.summary:
`POST /me/inbox/bulk` — bulk inbox transitions
(mark-all-seen / snooze-all / done-all / inbox-all). Used by the
list-header bulk action menu in the workbench. Audited under the
`BULK_INBOX_*` vocabulary so the audit log can answer "who did
the mass dismiss?" without scanning the per-row writes.

400.description: Batch too large / snooze without deadline

post.summary:
`POST /me/inbox/seen` — bulk-mark issues read. Idempotent. The
store upserts one `dp_user_issue_state` row per id, setting
`last_seen_version` from `dp_issues.version` (so the UI never
has to know the version itself).

400.description: Too many issue ids in one batch

patch.description:
The body's `status` and `snoozed_until` are written verbatim;
see [`SetInboxStateRequest`] for the consistency contract.

Returns the resulting row so the UI can confirm without a
second round-trip.

get.summary: `GET /me/pins` — caller's pins, ordered by `position` ascending.
get.description:
Audit: not audited. Pins are personal UI state and `GET` traffic
would swamp the audit log without operational value (§6.5 only
pins the three mutation verbs).

post.summary: `POST /me/pins` — append a pin to the caller's list.
post.description:
* Position is server-assigned (`len(existing)`).
* Returns `400 pin_cap_exceeded` if the caller already has
  [`PIN_CAP`] pins (§13.5).
* Returns `409 pin_exists` if the `(kind, target_id)` row is
  already in the caller's pins (idempotent re-pinning, §6.4 /
  the composite-PK note in [`dp_domain::store::Store::add_pin`]).
* Audit: writes [`audit::PIN_ADD`] with target
  `"<kind>:<target_id>"` after the row lands.

409.description: Pin already exists for this caller

put.summary: `PUT /me/pins/order` — atomically rewrite the caller's pin order.
put.description:
The request body's `order` must exactly cover the caller's
current pin set; missing or extra `(kind, target_id)` entries
surface as `400 reorder_set_mismatch`. The store applies the
rewrite in one transaction so a concurrent reader cannot observe
a partial reorder (§6.3 row-by-row comment, §13 atomicity rules).

Audit: writes one [`audit::PIN_REORDER`] row with target
`"count:<n>"` (n = number of pins reordered). We do **not** dump
the full key list into the audit target — that would balloon the
`dp_audit_log.target` column past the small-text comfort zone
and the audit verb is meaningful at row granularity (one row =
one reorder operation).

400.description: `order` does not exactly cover the caller's pins

delete.description:
Returns `404 pin_not_found` when the row is not in the caller's
pin set. Audit: writes [`audit::PIN_REMOVE`] after the row is
gone.

Note on positions: the §6.3 schema does not auto-compact `position`
values on delete (the store does not renumber). The next
[`reorder_pins`](crate::pins::reorder_pins) call is what compacts
the gap.

get.summary:
`GET /me/queue` — the caller's inbox. The default landing view
for the triage page (`linear-projects-idea.md` §3.8 / §5.4).
get.description:
Returns issues that the caller has not dismissed (`status <>
'done'`) and that are not currently snoozed (`status <>
'snoozed' OR snoozed_until < now()`). Rows that have never
been touched surface as default-state ("inbox", unread until
the user opens the peek panel).

Accepts the same filter set as `GET /issues` so the smart-view
rail can pre-narrow ("My queue · phoenix only", etc.).

Each row carries an `unread` boolean — `true` when
`dp_issues.version > last_seen_version`. The frontend renders
an indicator and uses `POST /me/inbox/seen` to clear it when
the user opens the row in the peek panel.

parameters.name: untriaged
parameters.description: Restrict to rows with no assignee and no label

get.summary: `GET /me/tags` — caller-owned or caller-is-scope-member tags.
get.description:
Convenience over `GET /tags` for the new-tag picker and the
"my tags" sidebar group. Returns the same row shape; the
filter is "the viewer is a scope member" (which for user-scope
= owner, for team/org-scope = membership).

parameters.name: include_archived
parameters.description: Include archived tags in the response. Default `false`.

200.description: Tags caller owns or is a scope member of

get.summary:
`GET /orgs` — every org dev-pulse has observed. (Stage 9 will
narrow to "orgs the principal can see"; stage 4 returns all.)

`GET /reports/freshness` — the data-freshness probe. Returns the
same envelope as the report routes but with `rows: null` so the
UI's "data as of …" widget can poll a single endpoint without
paying for an event scan.
get.description:
The resolved window is still echoed back (defaulting to
`last_7_days` UTC) so the response shape is uniform.

get.summary:
`GET /reports/home-org-split` — the SCOPE §7 cross-org executive
view. Always uses the [`ScopeMode::PerOrgSplit`] lens regardless
of what the request says (the route only makes sense in that
mode); each output row is one `(user, org)` bucket with the
count of distinct events the user is credited on in that org.

`GET /reports/issues` — §5.10 aggregate metrics over
`dp_issues`. Authorisation: `("issues", "read")`. The filter
scope is intersected with the caller's `org_ids` at the
handler boundary.

`GET /reports/org/:org_id` — counts for one org. The path
`:org_id` is forced into `request.orgs` (single-element) so the
`single_org` lens has the org to filter on regardless of what
the query string carried.

200.description: Counts for the org in the requested lens

get.summary:
`GET /reports/team/:team_id` — counts narrowed to one team
(passed through to the store via `request.teams`). Per-team
`group_by=team` is rejected in this stage; the route still
supports the other group-bys.

200.description: Counts for the team in the requested lens

get.summary:
`GET /reports/user/:user_id` — counts for one user across the
requested orgs / window / roles. The path `:user_id` is pushed
onto `request.users` so the query string can omit it (the path
is authoritative).

200.description: Counts for the user in the requested lens

get.summary:
`GET /repos` — paginated repo list with open-issue counts. Reads
only; not audited (low-sensitivity directory traversal, same
rationale as `GET /users` in [`crate::directory`]).

post.summary:
`POST /repos/{id}/sync` — operator-triggered per-repo
reconciler tick. Idempotent: if the scheduler is already
running a tick the call coalesces and the body is still
`{ "queued": true }` (the user's *intent* is queued even if
the scheduler decided to coalesce against an in-flight run).
Authorisation: `("repos", "sync")` — the one new auth pair in
slice 2.

503.description: Reconciler scheduler not configured in this deployment

get.summary:
`GET /repos/{id}/sync-status` — sync freshness badge data.
Authorisation: `("repos", "read")`.

`GET /repos/{repo_id}/issues/{number}` — single issue via the
canonical deep-link shape audit log entries already record.

parameters.name: include_archived
parameters.description: Include archived tags in the response. Default `false`.

200.description: Visible tags with viewer-filtered link counts

post.description:
* Caller must be a scope member of the requested scope, else
  `403 tag_scope_member_required`.
* Case-insensitive name uniqueness per scope is a DB-level
  expression index — a clash surfaces as
  `409 tag_name_conflict`.
* Audit: writes [`audit::TAG_CREATE`] with target
  `"<scope_kind>:<scope_id>:<tag_id>"`.

403.description: Caller is not a member of the requested scope

409.description: Tag name already in use for this scope

get.summary: `GET /tags/{id}` — single tag, plus a page of its visible links.

404.description: Tag does not exist or is invisible to caller

patch.summary:
`PATCH /tags/{id}` — rename / recolour / set description /
archive. Mutually-exclusive verb mapping:
patch.description:
* If `archived` is set: emits [`audit::TAG_ARCHIVE`] (regardless
  of whether other fields are also patched in the same request).
* Otherwise emits [`audit::TAG_UPDATE`].

The two-verb split lets the audit log answer "when did this
tag retire?" with one query (`WHERE action = 'tag.archive'
AND target LIKE '<tag_id>'`) without scanning every
`tag.update` row.

403.description: Caller is not a scope member

404.description: Tag does not exist or is invisible

409.description: Tag name not unique within scope

post.summary:
`POST /tags/{id}/links` — batch link, transactional all-or-
nothing per §7.5.
post.description:
Per-item validation (pre-commit):
* `target_id` must not duplicate an existing link of the same
  `kind` on this tag (`duplicate`).
* `target_id` must not duplicate another row in the same
  batch (`duplicate_in_batch`).

On any per-item failure the response is `422 batch_rejected`
with an `items: [{index, code, message}, ...]` array and
**nothing is committed**. On success, one audit row per link
is written per §7.6, and `LinkBatchResponse.warning` is set
when the post-commit link count exceeds
[`TAG_LINK_WARN_THRESHOLD`] (§13.5).

403.description: Caller is not a scope member

404.description: Tag does not exist or is invisible

delete.description:
Same per-item error surface as link: items that do not match
a live `(kind, target_id)` on the tag come back as
`code = "not_linked"` and the whole batch is rejected (no
partial unlinks). One `tag.unlink` audit row per detached
link.

403.description: Caller is not a scope member

404.description: Tag does not exist or is invisible

get.summary: `GET /teams?org_id=…` — teams inside one org.
`GET /users` — list users, optionally filtered to one org.
get.description:
Audit: writes one `report.read`-style row… actually `directory`
reads aren't in the v1 audit vocabulary (D4.4 only pins the eight
listed verbs). Listing users is a low-sensitivity read so we
intentionally do not audit it. The stage-4 mutation that does
audit is `POST /home-org`.

post.description:
The live receiver is `dp_fetcher::webhook::router::receive`;
authentication is the GitHub HMAC (`X-Hub-Signature-256`),
**not** a principal cookie. Stage 6 mirrors the route's
behaviour into the OpenAPI document so MCP / frontend clients
know it exists, without coupling `dp-fetcher` to utoipa.

This function is never invoked — `dp-server` mounts the real
router from `dp-fetcher` directly.

parameters.name: X-GitHub-Delivery
parameters.description: GitHub-issued delivery id; the inbox dedup key.

parameters.name: X-Hub-Signature-256
parameters.description: Hex-encoded `sha256=<digest>` HMAC over the raw body.

200.description: Delivery enqueued (or replayed — GitHub retries on any non-2xx)

400.description: Missing required header or unparseable JSON body

500.description: Persistence failure other than a replay conflict

Ack.description:
Trivial response shape — handlers that don't return data still
return a body so the UI doesn't switch on `204`.

AddPinRequest.description:
Body for `POST /me/pins`. The server picks the position
(`len(existing)`) and the `pinned_at` timestamp.

AppInstallBannerOrgDto.description:
One row in `GET /me/app-install-banner`.

`writes_available` mirrors the write-gate verdict for the
`(viewer, org)` pair so the frontend can render the §8.4
affordance without re-querying. `admin_copy_text` is the
§13.6 copy-able snippet; `manage_url` is the GitHub deep-link
(omitted when no App slug is configured).

admin_copy_text.description:
Copy-able admin text the viewer pastes into Slack / email
to ask their org admin to re-consent. Always present —
even for orgs where writes are already available, the
frontend hides the row but the text is harmless to carry.

manage_url.description:
GitHub-side deep-link to the install's permissions page.
`None` when no slug is configured or when no install
record exists for the org.

writes_available.description:
`true` iff a §8 issue write against this org would succeed
(deployment flag on AND install record allows
`issues: write`).

AppInstallBannerResponse.description:
Full §13.6 banner response.

`request_issues_write` mirrors the deployment-level flag so the
UI can render the "writes disabled in this deployment" mode
without inspecting each row's `writes_available`.

orgs.description:
One row per org the viewer is a member of (read through
`Store::list_memberships_for_user`). Orgs the viewer
cannot see at all are *not* included — the §15.11 access
gate is the single visibility check (§9 cross-ref).

request_issues_write.description:
`false` when [`GitHubAppConfig::request_issues_write`] is
off; the §8 surface is hard-disabled deployment-wide.

AppManifest.description:
The App's default permission set as declared in its manifest.

Each key is a GitHub permission resource (e.g. `"issues"`,
`"metadata"`); each value is the requested level (`"read"` or
`"write"`). [`app_manifest_permissions`] renders this from
[`GitHubAppConfig`] — `issues` is `"write"` when
[`GitHubAppConfig::request_issues_write`] is `true`, omitted
otherwise. The other resources are the read-only set the v1
reporting surface needs and do not change with the flag.

Used by deployment tooling and the (future) `/admin/app-manifest`
surface. Pure value; no side-effects.

default_permissions.description:
`resource -> level` map. Serialised in BTreeMap order so
the JSON is deterministic across runs (the OpenAPI
snapshot test cares).

slug.description:
App slug — informational, copied verbatim from
[`GitHubAppConfig::slug`]. Empty when unset.

BulkInboxOp.description:
Operation kind for [`BulkInboxRequest`]. One of mark-seen, snooze,
done, or restore-to-inbox — the four bulk actions the workbench
exposes from the list header.

BulkInboxRequest.description:
Body for `POST /me/inbox/bulk`. One operation applied to a batch
of issue ids.

touched.description:
Number of `dp_user_issue_state` rows touched (inserted +
updated). For `mark_all_seen` this is the upsert count from
the underlying `mark_issues_seen` call and is reported as the
length of the request batch (the store does not surface the
row count for that path today).

CountRow.description:
One aggregated count row. The `key` is stringified so the same
shape works for UUID group-bys (`User`, `Team`, `Repo`, `Org`) and
time-bucket group-bys (`Day`, `Week`, `Month` — RFC3339 instants).

count.description: Event count attributed to this bucket.

key.description: The bucket key, formatted as a string.

CreateIssueRequest.description:
Body for `POST /issues`. The repo to mutate is named explicitly
(there is no canonical row yet to derive it from).

repo_id.description: Internal repo id the new issue belongs to.

CreateIssueResponse.description:
Acknowledgement body for `POST /issues`. Returns the GitHub-side
number GitHub assigned (so the UI can deep-link immediately) and
echoes the actor's `repo_id` for symmetry with PATCH responses.

CreateTagRequest.description:
Body for `POST /tags`. Server picks `id`, `created_by`,
`created_at`. `scope_id` is required; the caller must be a
scope member or the request returns `403`.

name.description:
Display name. Case-insensitive uniqueness is enforced per
scope by the migration-0005 expression index — a clash
surfaces as `409 tag_name_conflict`.

scope_id.description:
Owning user/team/org id. For `user`-scope tags, must equal
the caller (returns `403 tag_scope_member_required`
otherwise).

DataAsOfDto.description:
`data_as_of` wire shape. Mirrors `dp_domain::freshness::DataAsOf`
but with the serde derives + utoipa schema the dp-domain type
intentionally lacks (dp-domain stays free of HTTP-shape concerns
per §0.6).

headline.description:
Convenience headline picked by lens (SCOPE §11.7). `None`
for `per_org_split` (the UI renders per row) and for
`single_org` / `all_orgs_combined` when the requested orgs
have no freshness entry yet.

per_org.description:
Per-org reconciler freshness. Absent orgs have never been
touched by the reconciler (treat as "pending", not "stale").

ExportEvent.description:
Per-event projection inside the export. Carries the event row
plus every role this user played on it — a squash-merge author
who later closed the same PR shows up once with
`roles: ["author", "closer"]`.

event_id.description: Event id (the join key inside the export).

roles.description: Every role the exported user played on this event.

FetchRunDto.description:
Wire row for `GET /admin/runs`. Mirrors [`FetchRun`] with serde
derives + `ToSchema` so the openapi document picks it up.

errors.description: Items that errored during the run.

finished.description: Wall-clock end (UTC). `None` while the run is in flight.

partial.description: `true` if the run finished but some items failed.

HomeOrgSplitRow.description:
One row of the `/reports/home-org-split` shape — per (user, org)
bucket, count of distinct events the user is credited on within
that org.

InboxStatusDto.description:
Wire form of [`InboxStatus`]. Lower-case to match the SQL form
declared in migration 0011.

IssueDatesDto.description:
Response body — the canonical post-upsert row. Mirrors
[`IssueDates`] one-for-one so the UI can render the freshly
stamped `updated_at` plus the most recent mirror outcome
(`mirror_synced_at` / `mirror_error`) without a second read.

mirror_node_id.description:
Projects v2 item node id, when mirroring has ever
succeeded for this row.

mirror_synced_at.description:
Wall-clock the most recent mirror attempt succeeded;
`null` until the first success.

IssueDto.description:
Full issue projection. Matches the shape the frontend's
`IssueDto` already declared (`api/client.ts`) so the existing
§8.3 detail pane wires up without DTO shape changes.

unread.description:
Per-caller unread flag — `true` when the issue's `version`
is newer than what the caller has marked seen. Only the
`/me/queue` endpoint populates this with a meaningful value;
every other endpoint emits `false`. Defaults to `false` so
older frontend clients that ignore the field render rows
the same as before.

total.description: Total matching the filter, ignoring pagination.

IssuePatch.description:
Field-level patch the PATCH handler forwards to GitHub. Every
field is optional — only `Some(_)` lanes are sent to GitHub. The
caller is the source of truth on what to mutate; the handler
performs no field-vs-field consistency checks.

assignees.description:
Replacement assignee logins. `None` leaves assignees
untouched.

body.description: New body (omitted when not changing; explicit `null` clears).

labels.description: Replacement label list. `None` leaves labels untouched.

state.description:
New state — `"open"` or `"closed"`. The handler routes this
to the `issue.close` / `issue.reopen` audit verbs.

IssueStateDto.description:
Wire form of [`IssueState`]. Lower-case to match GitHub's wire
form (`"open"` / `"closed"`).

rows.description: Bucketed rows, sorted by bucket asc.

bucket.description: Bucket label (repo id, org id, assignee login, or ISO date).

count.description: Row count contributing to the value (useful for medians).

value.description:
Metric value — count for throughput/wip/stale/untriaged,
median seconds for lead_time.

items.description:
Items to link. Transactional all-or-nothing; per-item
errors are returned via [`ApiError::Batch`] on rejection.

LinkBatchResponse.description:
Response from `POST /tags/{id}/links` on success — the
attached link rows plus an optional soft warning when the
tag's link count crosses [`TAG_LINK_WARN_THRESHOLD`] (§13.5).

linked.description: The persisted link rows in insertion order.

warning.description:
Optional advisory warning. `"tag_link_count_high"` when
the tag now holds more than the warning threshold — the
operation committed regardless (§13.5 "the response
carries the warning, the operation still commits").

LinkRequestItem.description:
One entry in a `POST /tags/{id}/links` request — what to
attach.

MarkSeenRequest.description:
Body for `POST /me/inbox/seen`. The server marks every listed
issue as read up to its current `version`. Empty list is a
no-op (`204`). Capped at 200 ids per request to keep the
SQL bind size sane — clients with more than that should
page their reads via the list endpoint anyway.

joined_at.description: When dev-pulse first observed this membership.

PatchIssueDatesRequest.description:
Body for `PATCH /issues/{id}/dates`. Both fields are optional —
`null` (or omitted) clears that side. The schema CHECK guards
`start_at <= due_at`; the handler surfaces violations as
`400 invalid_date_window`.

due_at.description: New due instant (inclusive). Omit / `null` to clear.

start_at.description: New start instant (inclusive). Omit / `null` to clear.

expected_version.description:
CAS token — the `dp_issues.version` the UI rendered the form
against. The §18.2 step 5 CAS misses if this is stale, and
the handler returns `409 stale_local_version`.

PinDto.description:
One row in `GET /me/pins`. Hydration of `target_id` to a full
repo / tag payload is a follow-up stage — for now the client
joins against `/orgs`, `/repos`, `/tags` itself.

position.description: Sidebar order. Lower comes first; assigned by the server.

PinKindDto.description:
Wire form of [`PinKind`]. Mirrors the lower-case strings in the
`dp_user_pins.kind` CHECK constraint (`'repo' | 'tag'`).

items.description: Total deliveries applied during the tick.

oneOf.description: The trigger coalesced into an in-flight tick.

RefreshResponse.description:
Response body for `POST /admin/refresh`. Variants are flattened
so a coalesce comes out as `{ "ran": false }` and a real tick
as `{ "ran": true, "items": …, "errors": …, "partial": … }`.

ReorderRequest.description:
Body for `PUT /me/pins/order`. The slice **must** exactly cover
the caller's current pin set — extra / missing entries are
rejected (`400 reorder_set_mismatch`).

order.description:
New order. Entry `i` becomes `position = i` after the
transaction commits.

RepoListResponse.description:
Paginated envelope. Carries `total` so the UI can render
`Showing X–Y of Z` without a second round-trip.

limit.description: Echoed back so the client can confirm what it asked for.

offset.description: Echoed back so the client can confirm what it asked for.

total.description: Total matching the filter, ignoring pagination.

RepoSummaryDto.description:
Row in `GET /repos`. Carries the join from `dp_orgs` so callers
don't have to round-trip for `org_login`, plus the two counters
the workflow list pane renders inline.

last_activity_at.description:
Most recent issue `updated_at`; `null` if the repo has no
issues yet.

open_issue_count.description: Number of open issues in this repo.

RepoSyncQueuedDto.description:
Wire envelope for `POST /repos/{id}/sync`. Always
`{ "queued": true }` on the 202 reply.

RepoSyncStatusDto.description:
Wire envelope for `GET /repos/{id}/sync-status`. See
`linear-projects-idea.md` §5.9. `queued` is `false` for now;
the scheduler does not expose per-repo in-flight introspection
so the badge UX treats "queued" as a transient client-side
flag set after a successful POST.

last_attempt_at.description:
When the last attempt finished — same value as
`last_synced_at` until the migration grows an
`attempted_at` column.

last_error.description: Last error, or `null` if the latest sync succeeded.

last_synced_at.description: When the last successful sync landed.

queued.description:
`true` if the scheduler is in the middle of reconciling
this repo. Currently always `false` — see module comment.

ReportResponse.description:
The envelope every report handler returns. `rows` is left as
[`serde_json::Value`] so the same struct serves the five report
shapes without forcing a per-handler enum — the OpenAPI doc
describes each handler's `rows` schema via per-route `body =
<Concrete>` overrides (added when the aggregator lands).

empty_reason.description:
Why the report has no rows, when the emptiness is the
*intentional* SCOPE-PROJECTS §7.7 outcome of the tag filter
not matching the requested metric's attribution column
(e.g. an `issue`-only tag queried against a commit metric).

`None` for every other empty result (window too tight,
no matching events, etc.) — those stay as `rows: []` so the
UI's existing empty-state copy still renders. Locked literal
is [`EMPTY_REASON_TAG_KIND_MISMATCH`].

resolved_window.description:
The UTC window the report ran against. Echoed verbatim from
[`resolve_window`] so the UI can label the report without
re-resolving (§0.4).

org_id.description: Org that becomes the new home for that user.

user_id.description: User to flip home org for.

SetInboxStateRequest.description:
Body for `PATCH /me/inbox/{issue_id}`. Either field may be
absent; an empty body leaves the row untouched (still upserted
at default values if it did not exist).

Consistency between `status` and `snoozed_until` is the caller's
responsibility — the server does not refuse `status = Inbox`
with `snoozed_until = Some(_)` so the UI can clear the snooze
by setting the status alone without a second round-trip.

snoozed_until.description: New snooze deadline. Use explicit `null` to clear.

oneOf.description:
New status (defaults to existing value when absent — for a
fresh row this means [`InboxStatusDto::Inbox`]).

TagDetailResponse.description:
`GET /tags/{id}` response: the tag plus a *page* of its links
(§7.5: "links are paginated separately (`?links_page=…`) to
keep a single response bounded even for tags near the §13.5
500-link soft warning").

links.description: One page of links — only those visible to the viewer.

links_page.description: Zero-based page index of the returned slice.

TagDto.description:
Tag row carried back to the client. Mirrors [`Tag`] but the
three nullable `scope_*_id` columns are collapsed into a single
`scope_id` — the discriminator + id is enough on the wire, and
matches how the frontend renders it.

visible_link_count.description:
**Viewer-visible** link count — never the true total
(§7.4). Populated by every list / get path.

TagLinkDto.description:
One link row carried back to the client. Mirrors [`TagLink`]
but collapses the four `target_*_id` columns into a single
`target_id` paired with [`kind`](Self::kind).

target_id.description: Linked repo / issue / user / team id per [`kind`](Self::kind).

TagLinkKindDto.description: Wire form of [`TagLinkKind`] — `repo | issue | user | team`.

TimelineEntryDto.description:
Wire form of an issue-timeline row. The shape mirrors §5.6 —
the peek panel renders this as a vertical activity strip.

total.description: Total matching the filter, ignoring pagination.

UnlinkBatchRequest.description:
Body for `DELETE /tags/{id}/links` — batch unlink. Same
`(kind, target_id)` shape as link — IDs are resolved on the
server inside the same transaction so a partial unlink is
impossible.

UpdateTagRequest.description:
Body for `PATCH /tags/{id}`. Every field is optional; missing
fields are left unchanged. Setting `archived_at: Some(true)`
archives the tag (§7.4 — no hard delete); `Some(false)`
un-archives.

archived.description:
`Some(true)` archives, `Some(false)` un-archives, `None`
leaves the archive bit alone.

description.description:
Set or clear the description.
`None` leaves untouched; `Some(None)` clears.

github_id.description: GitHub numeric user id (stable across renames).

UserExport.description:
Top-level shape emitted by `GET /admin/users/:id/export`.
Documented for the openapi schema even though the response is
served as a chunked stream — the wire JSON parses to this type.

events.description: Every event this user is credited on, ordered by `ts ASC`.

user.description: The user row (already pseudonymised if previously deleted).

UserIssueStateDto.description:
One row in the inbox state table. Echoed back by the
PATCH handler so the UI can confirm the write without a
follow-up GET.

last_seen_version.description: Highest `dp_issues.version` the caller has marked seen.

snoozed_until.description: Wake-up instant for snoozed rows. `None` for inbox / done.
